evidence: normalizeCreateTable only trims whitespace and ';', and the runner inserts a migration_log row (AUTO_INCREMENT id) per migration, so adding a migration changes AUTO_INCREMENT=N in the snapshot with no schema change. Stripping the clause is the right fix; the problem is canonicalization, not two sources of truth.
guidance_note: When writing a schema snapshot canary, normalize every row-count-dependent table option (AUTO_INCREMENT) before checking it in, and rerun the canary after adding a migration to prove it is stable.

evidence: The hunk shows report.IntegrityCheck = "ok" set before any check runs, and the smoke-failure path returns early, so the report claims an integrity check that never ran. The agent set each status only after its check runs and used 'skipped' on the short-circuit.
guidance_note: Never pre-initialize a status field to a success value; assign it only where the check completes, and give every early return its own explicit status.

evidence: adoptPreGooseWorkspace creates goose_db_version, seeds rows and deletes meta.schema_version without a commit, and the first per-migration DOLT_COMMIT('-Am') would sweep those changes in. A dedicated adoption commit is the right fix; single-enforcer does not describe commit isolation.
guidance_note: When introducing per-unit commits, list every working-set mutation that runs before the first unit and commit or reject each one, so no unit's commit absorbs unrelated state.

evidence: The comment says '.7 (structured stderr events) will replace the current name k=v plain text with JSON', but emitMigrationEvent already marshals JSON. The comment was rewritten to describe the current format.
guidance_note: Before pushing a multi-step feature, grep for comments that refer to future steps ('until then', step ids like .7) and rewrite the ones whose step has already landed.

evidence: The test docstring says it pins floor == codeVersion, but it writes the literal "1" while codeVersion is 3, so the boundary it claims to test is never exercised. The fix uses strconv.FormatInt(codeVersion, 10). This is a wrong test fixture, not a structure-vs-behavior question.
guidance_note: In a boundary test, build the boundary value from the constant that defines it, never from a literal that happened to equal it when the test was written.

evidence: The runner emits event="migrate.commit" while test strings and the helper name said 'migrate.committed'. The agent renamed the strings and the helper. The packet does not show that rename's diff, so it cannot confirm whether it split the TestMigrationLogSuccessRow docstring later flagged in F37/F49.
guidance_note: Name test helpers and assertion strings from the runtime constant they parse, so a test cannot drift from the event name it is checking.

evidence: The hunk shows a commitWorkingSet failure only emitting quarantine.commit_failed before returning me unchanged, so a reverted workspace could lose its quarantine with no error surfaced. The fix wrapped it into me.Cause. The same hunk shows the identical swallow on recordQuarantine failure a few lines up, which the fix left alone (F11). The law that applies is no-silent-failure, not single-enforcer.
guidance_note: When fixing one swallowed error in a function, fix every sibling error branch in that function in the same commit; the recordQuarantine branch was visible in the same hunk.

evidence: runMigrations makes per-migration, adoption and quarantine commits, so 'Commits the working set exactly once' is false. Accepting was right, but the claimed fix did not stick: F31 re-raised the same sentence in round 4, and the 1cb7c82 diff still removes 'Commits the working set exactly once if anything changed.'
guidance_note: Before replying 'Resolved in <sha>', check that the cited commit's diff actually contains the change, for example by running git show <sha> -- <file> and grepping for the old text.

evidence: The smokeProbes comment promises one probe per application table, but migration_log is in applicationTables and the snapshot and missing from the probes. The agent added the probe. The fix kept two manually synced lists instead of deriving one from the other, which is the actual one-source-of-truth problem.
guidance_note: When a comment promises that two lists stay in parity, derive one from the other or add a test that asserts the parity, instead of relying on 'new table, add to both'.

evidence: SmokeTest holds formatRecoveryHint output, a multi-word string (F53 shows report.SmokeTest = hint), yet the text line prints it with %s among key=value tokens. Switching to %q keeps it one token. This is output escaping, not a type-modeling issue.
guidance_note: When adding a free-form string field to a key=value text line, quote it (%q) at the moment you add it.

evidence: The agent's own reply calls this the 'sister case to the commitWorkingSet failure path that 1a78b84 surfaced': the recordQuarantine-failure branch sat directly above the branch F7's fix changed, and it still returned me unchanged. This cost a round.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags one swallowed error, scan the whole function for every branch that emits a *_failed event and then returns the unmodified error, and fix them together.

evidence: The comment says '(or .go)' can be dropped into the directory, but the embed loads only *.sql, so Go migrations need WithGoMigrations registration. The comment was corrected.
guidance_note: Check every 'add X by doing Y' doc comment against the mechanism next to it; here the embed pattern contradicted the comment.

evidence: The docstring says 'highest applied version' but the query orders by id DESC, i.e. most recently inserted. The agent reasonably kept the query, since the recovery hint wants the latest applied, and fixed the wording.

The code was 'b, _ := json.Marshal(m)' over map[string]any, so a marshal failure would print an empty line and break the one-JSON-object-per-line contract stated in the doc. A fallback JSON line carrying _emit_error keeps the contract.
guidance_note: Never discard an error with _ in a helper whose doc promises an output contract; handle it at the point of writing.

evidence: The comment says the test 'uses the go list tool', but runGrepInProductionCode uses os.ReadDir. The drift predates F9's edit to that docstring, which only added the smoke.go exception paragraph.
guidance_note: When editing a function's docstring for one reason, reread the rest of it against the current implementation before committing.

evidence: runSmokeTests calls rows.Close() and discards its error, so a probe whose failure only shows at Close reports ok. The fix returns Close errors with the probe name. This is a swallowed error, not a type issue.
guidance_note: In health-probe code, check every error-returning call, including Close and rows.Err; an unchecked error in a probe is a false 'ok'.

evidence: Every Open, including the doctor's own Open, called CreateCheckpoint at current HEAD, so ResetToPreMigration's checkpoints[0] was always a no-op target and the recovery feature could never work. In 1cb7c82 the checkpoint is created only when adoption or pending work exists. That fix left the runMigrations docstring stale (F56), was not applied to the dry-run path (F51/F52), and made the pre-baseline bootstrap checkpoint the usual reset target (F46/F54).
guidance_note: When designing a 'reset to the last checkpoint' feature, trace the exact call path of the recovery command (here doctor opens the store first) and write a test that runs the real command end to end, which would have shown the no-op.

evidence: The 00003 comment promised running rows as a crash signal, but the runner only writes success and failure rows. In 1cb7c82 the comment was rewritten to the success/failure-only semantics.
guidance_note: When a schema comment describes a lifecycle (running, then success/failure), grep for the writer of each state before merging; a state with no writer is a doc bug or a missing feature.

evidence: runMigrations takes one CreateCheckpoint before the whole pending batch (the 1cb7c82 diff shows a single checkpoint before the loop). On a fresh or adopted workspace, a v3 failure therefore resets to a state before v2 created migration_quarantine. The agent's 'invariant by induction past v2' is false: v2 succeeding inside the same batch does not move the checkpoint. The round-6 suppressed comment confirms the same hole.
guidance_note: Before pushing back with an invariant argument, walk the reviewer's concrete sequence (fresh workspace, v1 and v2 succeed, v3 fails) through the code, specifically where the checkpoint is taken relative to the loop.

evidence: commitMigration called DOLT_COMMIT directly, bypassing retryTransientManifestReadOnly, the store's single transient-commit retry policy. 1cb7c82 wraps the call in that retry.
guidance_note: When adding a new write path that commits, find the store's existing commit or retry boundary and route through it rather than issuing the raw CALL.

evidence: With codeVersion 3, applying the injected v99993 leaves goose top above the binary, which checkCompatWindow refuses, so the test does not model DB-behind-binary. The test was renamed and given a codeVersion override. The test shows the runner will apply an out-of-window migration, which is F41's point.
guidance_note: Name a skew test after the inequality it sets up, and assert that a follow-up Open still succeeds so a scenario that leaves the workspace out of window fails the test.

evidence: The entries claimed an older binary can operate workspaces at v2/v3, but checkCompatWindow also refuses top > codeVersion. 1cb7c82 rewrote the block to say min_code_version only sets the floor.
guidance_note: When documenting a compatibility gate, state every condition the gate checks; the comment described the floor check and omitted the top-version check.

evidence: resolveDoctorAccessMode gained the reset flag but the table test had no case for it. 1cb7c82 added two cases, as the app_bootstrap_test.go diff shows.
guidance_note: When adding a flag to a function that has a table-driven test, add the row in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk ends at versionFromGooseError, and the ApplyVersion error path passes m.version directly (1cb7c82 diff: revertWithQuarantine(ctx, safety, "up", m.version, ...)). The agent defended collectSettledVersions, a different function, so the pushback answered a claim the reviewer never made.
guidance_note: Before pushing back on 'this helper is unused', name the helper from the hunk's anchor line and grep for that exact identifier.

evidence: On a fresh workspace v1 and v2 run before v3 creates migration_log, so every bootstrap emitted migration_log.write_failed; the original comment even says 'fails silently via the event log'. 1cb7c82 probes tableExists first. That probe also returns silently on a tableExists error, which is a minor new swallow.
guidance_note: Don't ship a code path that is known to emit failure events on the happy path; gate the write on the precondition when you write it.

evidence: DSN construction uses the active Dolt branch, not a pinned master, and DOLT_RESET acts on the active branch, so '(master)' was wrong. 1cb7c82 rewrote the docstring.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a factual claim in one comment, grep the package for the same claim; the 'master' wording also sat in migration_quarantine.go (F34).

evidence: This re-raises F17 in round 4, which ran at 20:07 before the agent answered round 3 at 20:21. The flag is a false positive: the unconditional CreateCheckpoint is round-0 code (visible in F3's hunk), and 8584462's diff shows only skew_test.go re-added as a new file, so the head was rewritten rather than the logic changed.

resetToPreMigrationLocked resets first and then calls recordQuarantine, so a checkpoint taken before the first migration run (the bootstrap checkpoint) leaves HEAD reset with no quarantine. The agent's 'only when v2 itself failed' ignores successful bootstraps, whose checkpoint is pre-baseline. The flag is a false positive: this function is round-0 code, and 8584462 only re-added skew_test.go.
guidance_note: For a destructive multi-step operation, check every later step's preconditions on the post-reset state before performing the reset, and test the operation against the oldest checkpoint the system can produce.

evidence: The commit-failure branch passed phase "up" and m.version to revertWithQuarantine, which would permanently exclude a migration whose body succeeded. 1cb7c82 passes "commit" and version 0, so the migration is reverted but not quarantined. The flag is a false positive: the branch is pre-review code.
guidance_note: When wiring failure paths into a quarantine mechanism, decide per failure phase whether the migration body is at fault, and quarantine only those phases.

evidence: This duplicates F20, raised before the agent had answered round 3, and both were fixed by the same retry wrap in 1cb7c82. The flag is a false positive: commitMigration is unchanged pre-review code.

F8 was answered 'Resolved in 30347c6' with this same topology rewrite, yet round 4's hunk still shows 'Commits the working set exactly once', and the 1cb7c82 diff is what finally deletes that sentence. The packet cannot show whether 30347c6 never contained the edit or a later history rewrite (8584462) dropped it, but the claimed fix was not on the branch.
guidance_note: After pushing a batch of fixes, run git grep for each removed phrase on the pushed head before posting 'Resolved in <sha>' replies.

evidence: This duplicates F18 while round 3 was still unanswered, and the same 1cb7c82 comment rewrite fixes it. The flag is a false positive: the 00003 comment is original PR text.

This is the same hole as F19, and the agent pasted the same reply. A single checkpoint precedes the whole first-open batch, so a v3 failure resets past v2's quarantine table. The flag is a false positive: revertWithQuarantine's ordering is round-0 code.
guidance_note: When the same finding comes back from an independent review pass, re-derive the pushback from the code instead of re-posting the previous reply.

evidence: The ResetToPreMigration comment also said 'Reset master'; the 1cb7c82 diff of migration_quarantine.go rewrites it to 'active Dolt branch'. This is the same claim as F26 but raised before F26 was fixed, so it is not fix-caused, and the flag is a false positive (original comment).
guidance_note: When one comment's factual claim is shown wrong, grep the package for the same claim before replying.

evidence: This duplicates F26 at a neighbouring line and is fixed by the same 1cb7c82 docstring edit. The flag is a false positive: the comment is original.

ListCheckpoints does match pre-migrate-* across all branches, so a multi-branch workspace could reset to foreign history. The agent's claim that workspaces stay on one application branch is unverified in the packet, but the hazard needs a usage pattern it says does not exist. 1cb7c82 documents the limitation inline. The flag is a false positive: ListCheckpoints is original code.

The head of the TestMigrationLogSuccessRow docstring sat orphaned above parseMigrateCommitEvents. 1cb7c82 deleted those two lines rather than reuniting them with the docstring's tail, which stayed orphaned at line ~593 (F49). The flag is a false positive for 8584462, which only re-added skew_test.go; the packet does not show which earlier edit (possibly the F6 helper rename) split the docstring.
guidance_note: When removing an orphaned comment fragment, find where the rest of that comment lives and restore the whole thing, rather than deleting only the piece the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: This duplicates F23, raised before round 3 was answered, and is fixed by the same added test rows. The flag is a false positive.

The hunk shows ts and event set before caller fields are merged, so a caller key could overwrite them. 1cb7c82 merges first, skips reserved keys, and writes ts/event last. The F14 fix touched this function but did not introduce the ordering, which is visible unchanged in F14's hunk, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When a helper promises mandatory fields, write them after merging caller input.

evidence: The cleanup did 'delete(migrationMinCodeVersions, 3)' unconditionally, which would erase a future production entry. 1cb7c82 saves and restores the prior value. The flag is a false positive: skew_test.go appears as a new file in 8584462 only because history was rewritten, since it was reviewed in round 0.
guidance_note: When a test mutates a package-level map or var, capture the prior value and presence and restore exactly that in t.Cleanup.

evidence: The agent is right that the case needs a self-contradictory binary, but adding a migration without bumping codeVersion is exactly that, and F21's test showed the runner applying v99993 above codeVersion=3 and leaving a workspace the binary then refuses. The agent named the right cure, a check that registry versions and min_code_version are at most codeVersion, then did not add it. The flag is a false positive: the apply loop is original.
guidance_note: When a pushback concedes 'the right place for this invariant is a build-time check', add that test in the same reply instead of leaving the invariant unenforced.

evidence: This duplicates F22, fixed by the same 1cb7c82 comment rewrite shown in the compat_window.go diff. The flag is a false positive: the comment is original.
This duplicates F21; 1cb7c82 renames the test and adds a testBinaryCodeVersionOverride. The flag is a false positive: the test is original.

The comment said 'baseline + 00002', but 00003 also applies on first Open, and 1cb7c82 updates it. The flag is a false positive: the stale comment predates review, left behind when 00003 was added during PR development.
guidance_note: When adding a migration, grep tests for comments that enumerate the migration set ('baseline + 00002') and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The agent claims 'the safety checkpoint for failure-in-v3 was taken after v2 committed', but the 1cb7c82 diff shows one CreateCheckpoint before the whole pending loop, so on a fresh workspace v3's failure resets to pre-v1. The reviewer notes the tests already acknowledge this. The flag is a false positive: 1cb7c82 moved the checkpoint later in the function but did not change its position relative to the batch, so the hole is the original F19 one.
guidance_note: When asserting where a checkpoint was taken, quote the line from the current diff; this pushback contradicted the diff it was replying under.

evidence: Before 1cb7c82, the doctor's own Open always created the newest checkpoint at HEAD. After F17's fix stopped no-op checkpoints, checkpoints[0] on a workspace with no migrations since bootstrap is the pre-baseline bootstrap checkpoint, so the reset-then-recordQuarantine failure F28 described became the normal recovery path. The agent's 'only when v2 hadn't been committed' misses that the bootstrap checkpoint predates v2 even when bootstrap succeeded.
guidance_note: When changing which checkpoints exist, re-derive which one the recovery command will pick in each workspace shape (fresh-bootstrapped, adopted, upgraded), and test reset against each.

evidence: This time the reviewer said explicitly that 'the ApplyVersion error path passes the loop's m.version directly', and the agent again grep'd collectSettledVersions, not versionFromGooseError, and kept the dead helper. The flag is a false positive: versionFromGooseError is unchanged since round 0, and this is a re-raise of F24 after a misdirected pushback.
guidance_note: When a reviewer repeats a finding you dismissed, reread the hunk's last lines to confirm which symbol it is about before grepping.

evidence: A second orphaned docstring fragment ('// in ascending version order.') sat in the same test file that F37's fix edited. That fix removed only the fragment it was pointed at and did not sweep the file for the same mangling.
guidance_note: When one orphaned doc fragment turns up in a file, scan the whole file for comment lines that start lowercase or mid-sentence directly above a func.

evidence: 1cb7c82 deleted '// TestMigrationLogSuccessRow verifies that after a successful Open the' from above parseMigrateCommitEvents, and that line was exactly the missing head of the comment now flagged at line 593 ('// migration_log table contains at least one row...'). Restoring it would have closed both.
guidance_note: When deleting a comment fragment that names another symbol, move it to that symbol instead of deleting it.

evidence: The hunk shows 'if *resetPreMigration { return runDoctorResetToPreMigration(...) }' before --fix is handled, so a combined invocation silently drops the fixes. They are now mutually exclusive with an error. The flag is a false positive: this branch is original code, and 1cb7c82 only added test rows.
guidance_note: When adding a flag that returns early, decide its interaction with every existing flag and reject the combinations it would silently ignore.

evidence: F17's fix rested on the invariant that the newest pre-migrate checkpoint always precedes a real mutation, but the dry-run path still created a durable, pruning checkpoint. The agent's own reply restates that invariant. The reviewer named both the leftover branch and the eviction caused by pruning, and the 9904925 fix addressed only the leftover branch (F55).
guidance_note: When a fix establishes an invariant ('the newest checkpoint is pre-real-mutation'), list every caller of the primitive (dry-run included) and check each against it before pushing.

evidence: revertDryRun, the dry-run failure path, also leaves the validation checkpoint behind after pruning. It is the same unswept caller of F17's invariant as F51, and the same 9904925 cleanup helper fixes it.
guidance_note: Sweep both the success and failure exits of a mode when changing its resource lifecycle.

evidence: The reviewer says the CLI's CorruptionError JSON remediation still says 'lit doctor --fix integrity'. The agent replied only that the error message contains the reset hint and never addressed the remediation field, and the packet does not include the CLI classification code, so neither claim can be checked. The flag is a false positive: 9f5a9db only removed a lock file and edited .gitignore.
guidance_note: When pushing back, answer the specific artifact the reviewer named (here the structured remediation field) rather than an adjacent one (the message text).

evidence: This is the fourth raise. The reviewer states the post-F17-fix reality, 'The first successful Open leaves a pre-migrate-* checkpoint from before baseline/00002', so a successful bootstrap, not a failed v2, puts the reset target before migration_quarantine. The agent repeated the 'only when v2 itself failed' claim, which the scenario directly contradicts. The 9f5a9db flag itself is unrelated (a lock-file commit).
guidance_note: A finding raised three times by independent passes is a signal to build the reviewer's scenario as a test before replying.

evidence: F51's text already said 'CreateCheckpoint has already pruned older checkpoints ... avoid pruning/creating durable branches for dry-runs', yet 9904925 only deleted the dry-run branch afterward, so a real checkpoint was still evicted. fe4f1e7 moves dry-runs to a separate pre-migrate-dryrun prefix.
guidance_note: When a finding lists two consequences, map each one to a line of the fix before replying; the second consequence here (prune eviction) had no corresponding change.

evidence: 1cb7c82 added the no-work short-circuit but left the runMigrations docstring claiming 'Same operations every Open: create checkpoint, read quarantine, adopt...', and it added a new in-body dataflow-not-control-flow comment that contradicts it.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a function's control flow, reread that function's own docstring before pushing; invariants it states are the first thing a structural fix falsifies.

narrative: A large migration-runner PR with seven Copilot rounds. Round 4 ran on a rewritten head (8584462 shows skew_test.go as a new file) before round 3 was answered, so most of its ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flags are duplicates of pending findings, not fix-caused. The costly fix was 1cb7c82 for F17 (skip the checkpoint on no-op Opens): it left the runMigrations docstring contradicting the new flow (F56), missed the dry-run path (F51/F52, whose fix then missed the prune-eviction half the reviewer named, F55), and made the pre-baseline bootstrap checkpoint the default reset target (F46/F54). The agent pushed back four times on the quarantine-table-predates-checkpoint hole (F19/F33/F45, F28/F46/F54) with an argument the diff contradicts, and twice defended the wrong helper on the dead-code finding (F24/F47); the PR merged with both open. Round 6 contained only fix-caused findings plus rejected repeats.
guidance_observations: Pushbacks were re-posted verbatim across rounds instead of re-derived from the code, so one false invariant claim ('the checkpoint is taken after v2 committed') survived four independent raises and merged.
The F24/F47 pushbacks answered a different function than the hunk's anchor, which a grep for the anchored identifier would have caught.
A 'Resolved in <sha>' reply (F8 to 30347c6) was not on the branch two rounds later; replies should be posted only after confirming the change exists on the pushed head.

Fixes that establish a new invariant (F17: the newest checkpoint precedes a real mutation) were not swept across every caller of the primitive or checked against the function's own docstring, and that produced most of rounds 5 and 6.
The agent merged three minutes after round 6 while it still contained unresolved correct findings (F54, plus the dead helper from F47).
